title: Check Geek+ RMS overall page for system faults vs AGV system faults (and handle blank RMS due to firewall)
summary: Use the Geek+ RMS / fleet status web UI to confirm the overall page is reachable and that it correctly separates fault categories: “system faults” on the left and “AGV system faults” on the right. If the RMS page is blank, treat it as a reachability/firewall symptom. Use the left/right placement to interpret whether the issue is communication loss vs an AGV that was commanded to move but is not in progress.
when_to_use: When you need to verify that the Geek+ RMS overall/fleet status page is reachable and that it is showing the expected fault panels (left system faults vs right AGV system faults), including the specific symptom where the page appears blank due to firewall not being open.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Execute the RMS overall page reachability and fault-panel visibility check, and interpret left/right fault placement for communication-loss vs commanded-but-not-in-progress movement.
operator: Provide observed state context if needed (e.g., whether the RMS page is reachable from their environment).

access_required: Access to the Geek+ RMS / fleet status web UI (rms_ui)

visual_references.description: Overall System RMS page frame showing the expected layout: system faults on the left and active AGV system faults on the right; also includes the blank-page symptom when firewall is not open.

steps.title: Open the Geek+ RMS / fleet status web UI (RMS overall page)
steps.purpose: Establish whether the RMS overall page is reachable and can display fault panels.
steps.instruction: Open the Geek+ RMS / fleet status web UI (RMS / fleet status UI).
steps.expected_result: The RMS overall page loads (or you observe that it is blank).
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS overall page is visible and fault panels can be observed.
steps.failure_condition: The RMS overall page shows blank (no visible fault panels).

actions.label: Open RMS overall page
actions.exact_action: Open the Geek+ RMS / fleet status web UI (RMS / fleet status UI).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: This page should show RMS, but the firewall is not open, so it just kind of shows blank.

steps.title: Confirm the RMS page is not blank; if blank, treat as firewall/reachability symptom
steps.purpose: Differentiate between a true fault-panel absence vs a reachability/firewall issue.
steps.instruction: Check whether the RMS overall page shows content/fault panels. If it is blank, treat it as the firewall-not-open symptom described by the source.
steps.expected_result: Either (a) fault panels are visible, or (b) the page is blank consistent with firewall not being open.
steps.failure_condition: RMS remains blank (no visible system/AGV fault panels).

actions.label: Check for blank RMS
actions.exact_action: Confirm the page is not blank. If the page is blank, treat it as a firewall/reachability symptom consistent with the source statement that RMS shows blank when the firewall is not open.

stop_or_escalate_if: RMS remains blank (no visible system/AGV fault panels).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: This page should show RMS, but the firewall is not open, so it just kind of shows blank.

steps.title: Check left-side “system faults” panel
steps.purpose: Identify system-fault category visibility and use it for interpretation of communication-loss symptoms.
steps.instruction: On the RMS overall page, check the left side labeled area for “system faults”.
steps.expected_result: The left-side “system faults” area is visible and can be reviewed for any listed faults.
steps.healthy_condition: The left “system faults” panel is visible (fault rows/entries can be observed if present).
steps.failure_condition: The left “system faults” panel is not visible or the page layout does not match the expected left/right separation.

actions.label: Inspect left system faults panel
actions.exact_action: On the RMS overall page, check the left side labeled area for “system faults”.

stop_or_escalate_if: Fault placement/layout is not observable or does not match the expected left/right meaning described by the source.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: On the left, you'll see system faults...

steps.title: Check right-side “AGV system faults” panel
steps.purpose: Identify active AGV system faults and use it for interpretation of commanded-but-not-in-progress movement symptoms.
steps.instruction: On the RMS overall page, check the right side labeled area for “AGV system faults” (active AGV faults).
steps.expected_result: The right-side “AGV system faults” area is visible and can be reviewed for any listed faults.
steps.healthy_condition: The right “AGV system faults” panel is visible (fault rows/entries can be observed if present).
steps.failure_condition: The right “AGV system faults” panel is not visible or the page layout does not match the expected left/right separation.

actions.label: Inspect right AGV system faults panel
actions.exact_action: Check the right side labeled area for “AGV system faults” (active AGV faults).

stop_or_escalate_if: Fault placement/layout is not observable or does not match the expected left/right meaning described by the source.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: ...and on the right there's AGV system faults.

steps.title: Interpret left/right fault placement for communication loss vs commanded-but-not-in-progress movement
steps.purpose: Use the fault placement to understand the likely category of the underlying issue.
steps.instruction: Use the source mapping: if you lose communication with a chat, expect it on the left “system faults”; if you told an AGV to move but it hasn’t moved, expect it on the right “AGV system faults”.
steps.expected_result: You can map the observed fault placement to either communication-loss (left) or commanded-but-not-in-progress movement (right).
steps.healthy_condition: Observed faults align with the expected left/right meaning (left = communication loss; right = commanded move not in progress).
steps.failure_condition: Fault placement does not align with the expected left/right meaning described by the source.

actions.label: Map fault placement to meaning
actions.exact_action: Use the source mapping to interpret placement: if communication loss with a chat occurs, expect it on the left “system faults”; if an AGV was told to move but it has not moved/in progress, expect it on the right “AGV system faults”.

stop_or_escalate_if: Fault placement does not match the expected left/right meaning described by the source.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If we lose communication with one of the chats, it'll be on the left. If we told an AGV to move but it hasn't moved, it'll be on the right.

success_criteria: RMS overall page is reachable and not blank (fault panels visible).
Left “system faults” and right “AGV system faults” areas are observable on the RMS overall page.
Observed fault placement can be interpreted as communication loss (left) vs commanded-but-not-in-progress movement (right) using the source mapping.
healthy_conditions: RMS overall page shows the expected two fault areas: system faults on the left and active AGV system faults on the right.
If the RMS page is blank, it matches the firewall-not-open symptom described by the source.
failure_conditions: RMS remains blank (no visible system/AGV fault panels).
Left/right fault separation is not observable or does not align with the expected meaning (left = communication loss; right = commanded move not in progress).
escalation_guidance: If RMS remains blank (no visible system/AGV fault panels), escalate as a firewall/reachability issue consistent with the source symptom.
If the left/right fault placement does not match the expected meaning described by the source, escalate for further investigation of RMS fault categorization/communication behavior.
